questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) The multimedia centre of a school consists of a router, server, client computers and other computer networking devices. **Figure 1** below illustrates a block layout of some of the equipment in the multimedia centre.

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2026-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)

(i) Identify the physical network topology in Figure 1. (2 marks)

(ii) Is the network a peer-to-peer or a client-server network? Explain briefly. (2 marks)

(iii) Briefly describe the role of the following terms as used in computer networks.

- Router
- Server
- Client computers (comp1, comp2 ...) (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Topology (2 marks).** The **star topology**: the printer, the server and the five computers (Comp 1 to Comp 5) are each connected by their own cable to one central device, the hub, which is at the centre of the star.

**(ii) Type of network (2 marks).** It is a **client-server network**. The network has a dedicated server that provides services and resources (files, printing, internet access, security) to the client computers, and the clients depend on it; in a peer-to-peer network all computers have the same status and no dedicated server is used.

**(iii) Roles (6 marks, 2 each).**

- **Router:** a device that connects two or more different networks (for example the school LAN to the Internet) and forwards data packets between them, choosing the best path using the destination (IP) address.
- **Server:** a powerful computer that provides services and shares resources (files, printers, e-mail, databases, internet access) with the other computers on the network and manages user accounts and security.
- **Client computers:** the computers used by the users; they request services and resources from the server (open a file, print a document, browse the web) and display the results.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Briefly explain the role of each of the following in a computer system

(i) Network interface card (2 marks)

(ii) Video card (2 marks)

(iii) BIOS chip (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Network interface card, NIC (2 marks).** It is the circuit board (or chip) that connects a computer to a network, wired or wireless. It provides the physical connection, converts the computer's data into signals suitable for the network medium (and back), and carries the unique MAC address that identifies the computer on the network.

**(ii) Video card (2 marks).** Also called graphics card or graphics adapter. It receives the data to be displayed from the CPU, processes it (with its own graphics processor and video memory) and converts it into the signals sent to the monitor, so that text, pictures and video are displayed.

**(iii) BIOS chip (2 marks).** BIOS means Basic Input/Output System. This chip (a ROM or flash memory on the motherboard) stores the start-up instructions that run when the computer is switched on: it checks the hardware (power-on self-test), identifies the connected devices and loads the operating system from the disk into RAM. It also provides basic input/output routines and holds the hardware settings.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Write in full the acronyms:

- ROM
- RAM (2 marks)

(ii) What is the difference between ROM and RAM in terms of what conditions must be met for them to hold their data? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Acronyms (2 marks).**

- ROM = **Read Only Memory**
- RAM = **Random Access Memory**

**(ii) Difference (2 marks).** **ROM is non-volatile**: it keeps its data permanently, even when the power is switched off, so no power supply is needed for it to hold its data. **RAM is volatile**: it holds its data only while the computer is switched on and a continuous electric power supply is maintained; when the power is cut, the content of RAM is lost.
